paper_role: mechanistic Palmer extension; not a rescue analysis for Paper 2

previously_known: Palmer colonies have progressively concentrated into fewer effective breeding groups.
Larger breeding groups show higher chick output per pair under a frozen proportional-productivity null.
Matched pre-extinction chick performance is too sparse and non-confirmatory.
The new cross-lag redistribution coefficients defined here have not been computed before this contract.
provenance_boundary.claim: This is a prospectively frozen new endpoint on previously inspected source data, not a fully outcome-blind preregistration.

already_known: Performance-based public information is established in colonial seabirds such as black-legged kittiwakes.
A 2024 Adelie penguin study at Pointe Geologie reported a strong association between colony breeding success and one-year-lagged growth that was interpreted as coherent with public-information use.
A 2025 Palmer-region study showed that snow, aspect and geomorphology are associated with sub-colony persistence and extinction.
therefore_not_novel: Claiming the first evidence that penguins may use conspecific reproductive performance.
Claiming that one-year-lagged breeding success and colony growth are associated in Adelie penguins.
Claiming that physical breeding habitat is irrelevant.
literature_boundary.target_novelty: Test whether dynamic reproductive state predicts subsequent within-island redistribution at Palmer after removing shared island-year forcing, prior colony size and persistent colony identity, and determine whether the lag profile is immediate or shows a delayed recruitment echo.

season_and_join_rules.adult_season: calendar year of November breeding-pair census
season_and_join_rules.chick_season: for January chick census, season_start_year = calendar year(time) - 1
season_and_join_rules.duplicate_policy: Collapse exact duplicate chick rows; exclude ambiguous duplicate keys with discordant numeric values; never average discordant duplicates.
season_and_join_rules.adult_size_source: Use the independent November adult census breeding-pair count, not the breeding-pair denominator copied into the chick dataset.

performance_state.eligibility: island-season with at least 3 matched colony codes, positive island total adult pairs, positive island total chicks, and finite nonnegative colony chick counts
performance_state.standardization: Within each eligible island-season, z-standardize the Pearson residual across matched colony codes; call this S_i,t.
performance_state.interpretation: S_i,t is relative reproductive performance conditional on contemporaneous group size and shared island-season conditions.

redistribution_outcome.colony_growth: G_i,u = log1p(adult_pairs_i,u+1) - log1p(adult_pairs_i,u) for adjacent annual censuses only
redistribution_outcome.relative_growth: Within each island and transition u -> u+1, subtract the mean G across eligible colony codes; call this R_i,u.
redistribution_outcome.prior_size_control: Within each island-transition risk set, z-standardize log1p(adult_pairs_i,u).
redistribution_outcome.reason: R removes shared island-scale annual forcing; prior-size control limits regression-to-the-mean artifacts.

model.form: R_i,u = beta_k * S_i,t + gamma * z_log_size_i,u + colony_code_fixed_effect + error, where u = t + k - 1
model.estimation: OLS on all complete matched rows for each lag separately
model.inference: Within each predictor island-season, permute S_i,t among eligible colony codes, refit the complete model, and compute a one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p-value for beta_k.

P1.name: performance-linked redistribution

direct_replication_endpoint.role: Replication/extension of an already published Adelie pattern; not the novel confirmatory gate.
direct_replication_endpoint.mechanical_coupling_warning: S_i,t and R_i,t both use adult_pairs_i,t. A positive beta_1 alone cannot support a new mechanism claim.

primary_bias_resistant_endpoint.rationale: S_i,t predicts redistribution during t+1 -> t+2, so predictor construction and growth denominator do not share the same adult census.
primary_bias_resistant_endpoint.decision: supported if beta_2 > 0 and one-sided within-island-season permutation p <= 0.05

P1.interpretation_if_supported: Dynamic reproductive state carries information about subsequent within-island redistribution beyond shared annual forcing, prior size and persistent colony identity. This is compatible with performance-linked settlement or retention but is not individual-level proof of public-information use.

P2.name: lag-profile mechanism diagnostic
P2.immediate_social_information_compatible_: beta_1 positive, with the explicit mechanical-coupling caveat; stronger support if beta_2 is also positive.

delayed_recruitment_echo.biological_basis: Adelie first breeding is commonly around ages 4-5, and natal-site attachment is strong enough that local chick production can generate a later cohort signal.
delayed_recruitment_echo.inference: Use the same within-island-season permutation draw across all lags in each Monte Carlo replicate, recompute C_recruit, and use a one-sided upper-tail p-value.
delayed_recruitment_echo.decision: supported if C_recruit > 0, p <= 0.05, and at least one of beta_4 or beta_5 is positive.

P2.interpretation: A 4-5 year peak is a local cohort/natal-recruitment echo, not a unique signature of public information. It must not be described as delayed public-information use.

secondary_sensitivities.exclude_litchfield: Repeat P1 lag-2 and P2 recruitment contrast after excluding Litchfield.
secondary_sensitivities.minimum_prior_size: Repeat after requiring adult_pairs at the outcome interval start >= 2.
secondary_sensitivities.low_chick_effort: Repeat after excluding predictor island-seasons with total chicks < 10.
secondary_sensitivities.success_metric: Repeat with within-island-season standardized log((chicks+0.5)/(expected_chicks+0.5)) instead of Pearson residual.
secondary_sensitivities.leave_one_island_out: Report beta_2 and C_recruit after removing each island in turn.

decision_matrix.beta1_only: Known-type one-year association replicated, but no evidence that performance state persists beyond the shared-denominator transition.
decision_matrix.beta2_supported: Performance-linked state predicts later redistribution under the bias-resistant endpoint.
decision_matrix.recruitment_echo_supported_only: Pattern is more consistent with delayed local cohort recruitment than immediate public-information redistribution.
decision_matrix.beta2_and_recruitment_echo_supported: Both short-term state-dependent redistribution and delayed local recruitment may contribute.
decision_matrix.neither_supported: Do not promote public-information or cohort-echo explanations for Palmer concentration.

claim_boundaries: Do not claim first evidence of public-information use in Adelie penguins.
Do not claim that dynamic state replaces topography or snow; Palmer fine-scale landscape effects are independently documented.
Do not infer individual movement, prospecting behavior or causal cue use from colony counts alone.
Do not call the 4-5 year lag a public-information signature.
Do not tune lags, success metrics, exclusions or alpha after the lagged outcomes are opened.
Paper 2 macro-scale negative results remain negative; this Palmer analysis is a separate mechanistic extension, not a post hoc rescue.
